summary: This is Installer No. 14, David Pierce's weekly Verge newsletter. It rounds up reader recommendations for money-management tools after Mint's shutdown, with YNAB and Copilot the top picks and spreadsheets a popular alternative. It also features Kevin Nguyen's homescreen and five writing apps, his media picks, reader recommendations, and a closing note on Tumblr's troubles.
one_line: David Pierce's Installer No. 14 collects reader-recommended budgeting apps after Mint's shutdown, plus Kevin Nguyen's writing apps, reader picks, and a Tumblr note.
key_facts: Mint is shutting down, which left many people looking for a new way to track budgets and spending; The Verge's Barbara Krasnoff compiled a list of Mint alternatives.
YNAB (You Need A Budget) was the most-recommended app by readers: it syncs accounts and cards, is an independent paid app without ads or credit card deals, and has a set of principles and systems.
Copilot is more polished than YNAB, praised for its design, dataviz tools and ease of use, but it is only available for iOS and Mac.
Other recommended apps, in rough order of popularity: Qapital, Buddy, Empower, HomeBank, Expenses, Quicken, EveryDollar, Nudget, Ledger, and Dime.
Many readers ended up using a spreadsheet in Excel or Google Sheets; Tiller and a Notion template were suggested to make that setup cleaner and more automatic.
Manual systems were described as a lot of work and easy to give up on; some suggested using a bank's built-in budget tools, with David Pierce hearing good things about SoFi's features.

David Pierce plans to try Copilot and build an 'epic 2024 budget spreadsheet'; he found YNAB great but struggled to keep up with it. His credit score once dropped after he signed up for too many personal finance apps.
Kevin Nguyen, a deputy editor at The Verge, uses five writing apps on his iPhone 15 Pro: iA Writer, Google Docs, Bear, Apple Notes, and Scrivener, each for a different purpose.
Kevin's writing-app habit was inspired by an interview with novelist Donna Tartt, who kept four cheap notebooks with different Beatles album covers; his wallpaper is Toshiro Mifune.

Kevin Nguyen's picks include Hiroshi Yoshimura's ambient record Surround, Ed Park's novel Same Bed Different Dreams, and the courtroom thriller Anatomy of a Fall, which premiered at New York Film Festival.

Reader recommendations include RetroAchievements, Spellrazor, The Kids of Rutherford County, Hidden Potential by Adam Grant, the Castro podcast app, Detroiters, Chants of Sennaar, the Beli app, 60 Songs That Explain the '90s, Scavengers Reign, and Kriegs.net wallpapers.
Pierce says Tumblr appears to be in trouble and had promised to work with ActivityPub; Matt Mullenweg, CEO of Automattic, which owns Tumblr, answered questions about its future that week.
